newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait gov't approves BA missile purchse-MP.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait gov't approves BA missile purchse-MP.

text.p: Kuwait's government has told parliament it had approved the purchase of British Aerospace Plc Sea Skua missiles, a senior parliamentarian said on Tuesday.

Adnan Abdul-Samad, member of parliament and chairman of parliament's Protection of Public Funds Committee, told Reuters acting Prime Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah had sent a message to parliament to inform it of the government's decision.
"The government's message says it has approved the purchase of the British missiles," Samad said.
Sheikh Sabah said in his message the government decision was based on a recommendation by a commission which had selected the Sea Skuas in competition MM-15 missiles made by France's Aerospatiale.
The specialised panel was the third to review the deal. The first picked the French missiles, while a second chose the Sea Skua. The members of the third panel did not form part of the previous two.
"It is up to parliament to decide the next move," Samad said.
Samad's committee said in July the government would be "politically responsible" if it decides to go ahead with the British missiles deal.
Industry experts have said the total Sea Skua package could be worth up to $150 million. Kuwait newspapers had earlier valued the deal at $90 million.
The government previously said its decision to buy the Sea Skuas was final, but it decided to form a Defence Ministry committee in response to strong criticism from parliament.
Kuwait intends to deploy the missiles on eight fast patrol boats ordered from France in 1995 in a contract worth $500 million.
